newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/yen eyes top, 115 blocks 115.70 retest.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/yen eyes top, 115 blocks 115.70 retest.

text.p: Dollar/yen remains on solid ground as long as it holds above 113.70, but analysts said tough short-term resistance near 115 offers an attractive selling objective.
"It looks like you've got to be short between 115 and 115.20 (yen), with a stop (buy order) above 115.30," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America.
"If we get above 115.30, the dollar could rally very strongly and take out the 115.60-115.80 resistance zone," Johnson added.
But overall dollar/yen's swift decline after failing to set a new short-term high above 115.70 on Monday points to range trading in the medium-term. Analysts said the dollar is probing for a top.

"While the short-term pullback holds above 113.70/80 yen, we will still allow for another push higher above 115.70 for the formation of the top of the range," said Darren Spain, global foreign exchange analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston.
The cycle high since the dollar fell to 110.62 yen on June 11 was 115.70 on June 12.
On Monday, the dollar came within a hair of retesting that high, touching 115.67 yen before a swift decline to 114.10 early Tuesday.

"You've got good support at the (114.00/10 yen) level, where we stopped last night. But the big level of support is 113.70. You've got to get below that level to continue the down trend," Johnson said.

Spain said dollar/yen is likely to remain between 113.70 and 115.70 in the medium term. A break above 115.70 targets resistance at 116.10, 117.05 and at the 200-day moving average, currently 117.55 yen.
Meanwhile, a series of lower highs and lows since the June 13 high at 1.7407 clouds the near-term dollar/mark outlook.
The shadow will only be lifted when the pattern is interrupted by a rise above the highs from Friday and Monday at 1.7320/25 marks, analysts said.

Not only would such a rise make new highs for the week, it would invalidate the downtrend line from 1.7407 marks and exceed the 61.8 percent retracement of the fall from that level to 1.7159 on Tuesday, they added.
At 1430 EDT/1830 GMT, the dollar was quoted at 1.7240/50 marks, up from 1.7235/45 at the open, and at 114.80/90 yen, up from 114.65/75.
